# 1102 — Custom URL scheme redirects pass the allowlist but Django blocks the 302

Build-start snapshot (batch order #2 of 6). Builds on top of #1101 (`091e0d2e`).
Full approved plan + challenge dispositions live on maestro Inbox item 1102.

## Objective
Widen the OAuth callback bounce to exactly the ONE scheme the allowlist vetted at `/begin`,
recorded in the OAuth state, re-checked at the callback, fail-closed to a 400 for anything else.
Owner ruling = option 1 (keep custom schemes working).

## Load-bearing (fail-closed structure — do NOT simplify)
- Stamp the vetted scheme at MINT time (`_vetted_bounce_scheme`, gated on `allowlisted=bool(custom_frontend_uri)`
  OR byte-equal `OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI`); the origin-derived else-branch stamps nothing.
- Re-check at the callback against `matchable_scheme(location)` before widening; derive scheme via
  `_split`/`matchable_scheme` (lowercased), never raw string-slicing.
- `except DisallowedRedirect: raise ValueException(400)` is the floor — also catches the >16 KB URL case.
- `_SchemeAwareRedirect` module-private in oauth.py, one call site (on_oauth_callback:464). Base set drops `ftp`.
- ADD the red-team negative test: `Origin: myapp://evil` + no redirect_uri → no frontend_scheme stamped → /callback → clean 400.
- Note #1101 landed: `matchable_scheme` goes through `_split`, so it inherits the dot-segment refusal.
